string.text: You achieved everything there was to achieve. The road was long, but you made it to a triumphant finale.
You have earned every possible Grim Raid achievement.
You stopped at nothing to obtain the most guarded knowledge from one of the Zone’s oldest stalkers. You may not believe everything you were told, but your accomplishments are undeniable.
The Renegades faction has been unlocked for the player.
You demonstrated to the military what “the bigger they are, the harder they fall” means. As a result, the Ministry of Defense decided to replace its remaining helicopters with cheaper models.
Mi-24s are being replaced with Mi-2s.
The hum, buzz, and hiss of anomalies can no longer frighten you. Your long experience working with detectors has made searching for and finding artifacts much easier.
Your accumulated experience has increased your chances of finding artifacts in anomalies after an emission.

Your deeds have made you a local legend, and you carry the confidence that only hard-won experience can give. Larger groups of stalkers, believing they will achieve more under your command, are now more willing to join you.
You can now recruit much larger groups of stalkers into your squad.

Whether through overcoming hardship yourself or reading other stalkers’ journals, you have come to understand many aspects of the Zone and its inhabitants. Perhaps it is time to share what you have learned with others.
From now on, you will find PDAs instead of memory cards.
Whether you are on an important mission or just killing time, defenseless wooden crates never escape your notice. Your obsessive crate-smashing has finally paid off.
Increased chance to find more items when smashing wooden crates.
You live by the rule that every item has a use and try to dismantle things down to the last screw. All that experience has made you remarkably handy; taking things apart is no longer difficult.
A small chance to recover an extra part when dismantling equipment.
Thanks to the knowledge and experience you gained while trying to build your own equipment, your crafting skills have reached maximum efficiency.

Over time, you learned to notice the little things in your enemies’ behavior, allowing you to imitate them more convincingly, as if you had mastered ninjutsu. Your disguise is more believable, and your odd behavior is now more likely to be seen as a trait of a quiet, friendly guest than as something suspicious.
Your behavior attracts far less suspicion when you wear another faction’s gear.
Your wealth has become well known among traders, who will always welcome you as a customer, regardless of your standing with their faction.

Waves of sinners rose from the deepest corners of the Zone and poured in every direction, disrupting an already fragile balance. Yet your resolve and determination helped you withstand them and uncover the mystery, finally putting the myth to rest.
The Sin faction has been unlocked for the player.

Recent events have finally reached a turning point for all sides in this conflict. After reaching an agreement, you chose to follow the course set by your unwavering resolve. For better or worse, you have proved that people can work with you.
The International Research Group (IRG) faction has been unlocked for the player.
The long, bloody war has finally come to an end. The victors write history—and take everything. Your faction emerged triumphant, and you were its trump card.
You received 50,000 rubles for taking part in the fighting.
You have turned out to be a truly unique stalker—someone who cannot simply surrender to the Zone... Probably? Enjoy what you have managed to achieve.

There may be no more worthy reward than this. Despite the hardships, trials, and twists of fate along the way, you still managed to achieve astonishing success. You are filled with pride and accomplishment, and the Zone has nothing left to surprise you with or challenge you. Perhaps it is time to move on to even greater things?
Now no one will doubt the stories of your adventures and achievements. Feel free to share a screenshot of this achievement.

Collecting souls is work too. Especially in the Zone, where bullets sharpen the scythe and the harvest shows no mercy. In a single minute, you turned a battlefield into a graveyard. Fast, cold-blooded, silent—as a true Reaper should be.
You remember noticing several interesting stashes during your previous travels.

A veteran among veterans is someone who did more than survive the Zone—they conquered it without a mark on their body. They are fearless, know what true resilience means, and know how not to let the Zone break them.
You found an encrypted marker in a scientist’s notes. Someone hid it for the person who would make it to the end.
An expert in all things concerning the Zone. A true expert doesn’t just study it—they read it like an open book.
An old PDA muttered some coordinates before it died. You wrote them down. Well, now it’s up to you.
Mastery cannot be drowned away. This stalker not only mastered all the Zone’s secrets, but also learned to play by its rules, leaving death not the slightest chance.
The stash of the stalker called Raven: myth or reality? Now you know for sure.

They say he was in Strelok’s group... But no one knows exactly where myth ends and truth begins. He became more than a legend: he became a symbol of immortality in the Zone, someone who cannot be defeated.
These stashes are for the chosen few. Their creator said, “Only the worthy will find them.”
To your surprise, the rumble of an approaching emission no longer has any psychological effect on you. Perhaps you have become as much at home in the Zone as a native.
You have a chance to survive an emission and a psi-storm while outside shelter.

A case where savagery leaves not only you, but the creatures themselves stunned. Three pseudogiants fell not to bullets, but to the iron in your hands. Madness? Perhaps. Courage? Absolutely. In the Zone, the fiercest survive—not the smartest.
You have a feeling the Zone rewards those who watch their surroundings carefully. You are one of them.
Sidorovich will buy even tin cans from you, but becoming his right hand takes more than knowing how to trade—you must become an important link in his chain.
In Sidorovich’s eyes, you have become a valuable partner, ready to strike a deal even for the dirtiest job.
Miser will give you the shirt off his back if he thinks you are worth it. Becoming his friend is like crossing an anomaly: you have to know exactly where to step and what to say.
Miser trusts you more than ordinary traders and is ready to pull his last item out of a crate for stalkers like you.
You now get not only good prices, but also the respect of the Barkeep.
The embodiment of Duty’s virtues: a stalker who not only obeys the law but is also ready to give their life for the common good.
The most valuable staff member understands the worth of knowledge and is willing to risk everything to obtain it. You have earned Professor Sakharov’s trust.
You can buy rarer goods from Sakharov and sell items to him on favorable terms.

A nasty bastard, the kind you rarely come across. You take jobs others won’t even hear out. Your moral boundaries are long gone, and dirty work has become routine. If a job reeks of danger and something vile, you’re in.
Someone left a message on the checkpoint wall: “Everything I have left is here. Take it—if you dare.”

This stalker is focused, reliable, and determined... and with a pistol in hand, he makes silence. Five targets in a minute—cold-blooded, precise, unhurried. The Zone doesn’t like people like that. It fears them.
Instinct tells you the Zone smiled on you somewhere... and hid something valuable.

A lover of kebabs or head cheese—it depends how you look at it. When others retreat at the sight of a boar herd, you charge forward, swinging an axe like you’re at a festive butchering. The Zone respects courage. Or madness. Sometimes they’re the same thing.
You remember leaving a mark on a tree... or was that someone else? Either way, it’s worth checking.

You have earned the respect of all the Zone’s key figures. Nothing stands in your way—not anomalies, mutants, or inflated prices. You know what every trader wants and can strike a deal with even the toughest haggler. In the Zone, reputation is worth more than artifacts.
With this level of trust in the Zone, you have become almost a legend. They won’t sell to you—they’ll make you an offer.
He goes on raids with his eyes closed—not because he is blind, but because he knows the Zone by touch. He doesn’t just survive; he works. Fast, precise, without fuss.
Something clicked in your head... maybe there was a stash there, maybe more than one.
For some people, artifacts are just shiny trinkets, while information is where true power lies. You, in turn, have proven yourself a reliable supplier of that information.
Information brokers will be glad to give you a small bonus for every PDA you sell them.

Six quests in one raid—you’re kidding, right? This stalker isn’t. He seems to sense what will happen, what people need, and where things are hidden. It’s not luck or fortune—it’s intuition honed to its limit by the Zone.
Your memory has sharpened—you’re sure you left something behind that hill, in the abandoned shed.

This stalker sees better in the dark... Or perhaps the darkness simply recognizes him and steps aside. Five successful raids under cover of night, when mutants are active and radiation is off the charts.
The information surfaced unexpectedly: a snippet of conversation, a shadow on the wall... now it means more.
On the back of an old dog tag are coordinates. Only an experienced stalker will know where to look.
On the back of an old dog tag are coordinates. Only an experienced stalker will understand where to look.
A veteran of the Zone is someone who has faced countless trials and kept their mind, if not their soul.
An expert of the Zone has studied every corner of it, every anomaly, and every mutant.
Someone marked a spot on your map with the note, “Don’t forget to pick this up.” Curious?
A master of the Zone is a stalker who does more than survive: they do it with skill.
You find an old helmet with coordinates scratched into it. There’s a stash there, and it’s definitely not for ordinary stalkers.
A legend of the Zone—every step leaves a mark, and every action sets an example for others.
The personal stash of a Zone veteran. It opens only to those who have truly achieved something.

After witnessing failed attempts to break through the psi-installations that had started operating again at Yantar and the Radar, you decided to take matters into your own hands. By disabling the installations, you finally broke the enemy’s defenses, and stalker squads surged toward the Zone’s center once more.
The routes through Yantar and the Radar are open again, making it easier for many stalkers to travel to the northern territories.
The Zone’s wildlife has learned to fear you: you earned the title of hunter by killing an unthinkable number of mutants. Your butchering skills have also reached the level of a true hunter.
Butchering dead mutants is now much faster.

You leave spent casings and stripped corpses in your wake. Your enemies know you as a ruthless killer. Those who survive the slaughter you leave behind will now part with their belongings much more readily, especially when their lives depend on it.
Captured stalkers may give you the coordinates of another stash.
Thanks to the tools you provided, gunsmiths can perform almost any upgrade to gear, suits, and weapons. You were also taught several ways to use consumables more effectively.
Extra consumables are now much more effective when repairing equipment.
You remember noticing several interesting stashes during your previous travels.

You know the phrase “what was yours is now ours” better than anyone; you have a nose for stashes hidden by stalkers. You have also witnessed the many tricks they use to protect their loot, so fake panels and hidden pockets can no longer keep their goods from you.
From time to time, you get lucky and find far more items in stalkers’ stashes.
